item.title: ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows
item.description:
ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows

ComfyUI has grown to include 779 nodes, expanding its capabilities to handle image, video, 3D, and language models along with the plumbing between them. The project has maintained an MIT license since 2023 and has accumulated over a million downloads. Its architecture is designed so that nothing is installed or fetched unless explicitly requested.

🧩 Core Capabilities

The node library supports a wide range of processing tasks, including:

  • Tiled and affine samplers, noise shaping, shift and schedule control, model quantizing, and LoRA stacks.
  • Crop-and-restore edits, edit regions, and specific model integrations like MiniMax H3 Image, Fibo 2.0, and BluePixel 4K.
  • Raw-style develop, film stocks, darkroom effects, and looks baked into LUTs.
  • Levels, LUTs, ACES and colour spaces, linear light, HDR video, and scopes and charts.
  • Skin, face, and subject masks, including masks drawn directly on the picture and subjects followed through a clip.
  • Filters and optics, layer stacks, layered PSD and TIFF files, and ControlNet preprocessors.

🎬 Video and 3D Features

Recent developments extend ComfyUI’s utility into complex video production and 3D generation:

  • Video Production: The Prompt Timeline allows long videos to be built a segment at a time. Features include upscaling, sparse attention, and Pika H3 Flex integration. The system supports video with sound, video super-resolution of any length, edits, transitions, titles, restored footage, face restoration through a shot, audio mixing, and beats.
  • 3D Generation: Capabilities include scenes, generated models, characters, meshes, blockouts, point cloud worlds, and Video Blueprint.

📚 Text and Logic Tools

The platform also includes utilities for prompt engineering and data handling:

  • Prompt terminology and a style library.
  • A system prompt library.
  • Support for text, lists, and dictionaries.

🚀 Availability and Resources

  • License: MIT (since 2023).
  • Downloads: Over a million.
  • Examples: 144 example workflows are provided.
  • Installation Model: Nothing installed, nothing fetched unless asked.

#ComfyUI #AIWorkflows #VideoGeneration #3DGeneration #OpenSource

item.title: MiniMax H3 Director: New ComfyUI Node for Multi-Clip Video Generation
item.description:
MiniMax H3 Director: New ComfyUI Node for Multi-Clip Video Generation

MiniMax H3 Director is a new ComfyUI node designed for long video and multi-segment generation. It integrates segment planning, conditional encoding, sampling, decoding, and export into a single interface, utilizing the official MiniMax H3 Image-to-Video and Reference-to-Video models alongside KSampler and AV separation decoding pipelines. The node natively outputs stereo audio.

🧩 How it works

The node manages a visual timeline for video generation, supporting several task types and advanced control over segmentation and transitions.

  • Segmentation and Editing: Users can upload video within the node to split, equally divide, or intelligently segment scenes using PySceneDetect. Split points are selectable and deletable, with a visual timeline previewing each segment’s range and thumbnail.
  • Grouped Keyframes: An independent first-last frame timeline allows multiple keyframe groups. Users can either write prompts for text-to-video or upload first/last frames (officially supporting last-frame-only uploads).
  • Inter-Segment Guidance: When enabled, empty groups use the last N frames of the previous segment for motion and audio continuity. Users can adjust duration via dragging and select specific groups to run.
  • Prompt Syntax: Prompts utilize <Picture N>, <Video K>, or <Audio J> tags (or @ references). The timeline preview and selection states remain synchronized with the prompts.
  • Reference Binding: For style-source video timelines, each segment’s source frame is automatically bound to <Video 1>. For reference-to-video tasks, additional reference images (up to 9) and audio (up to 3) can be attached per group.
  • Selective Sampling: When enabled, only checked segments or material groups are sampled. Unchecked segments can be filled with cache or source frames during export.
  • Audio Integration: Audio is generated in the same sampling pass as the visuals. For video-to-video and reference-video tasks, users can choose to generate sound, use original audio, or remain silent.
  • Reference Audio Slots: Users can select existing videos or local audio/video files. Selected videos immediately extract the first audio track as FLAC, saved directly to the input/ directory.

⚙️ Key details

The node supports various task types and integrates external modules to refine the generation pipeline. A semantic bridge and self-lift module can be attached to specific ports; if unconnected, the system behaves as a standard single-stage one-sampling process. When connected, the self-lift module transforms the process into a low-resolution prefix, 3D lift, and high-resolution finish, using Euler sampling at the director canvas resolution.

External Modules and Refinement

Module/Feature Functionality
Semantic Bridge Uses a student MLP to rewrite official conditional tokens. Weights are not distributed with the plugin and must be placed in models/semantic_bridge/.
Self-Lift Connects to the selflift port. Enables a multi-stage sampling process (low-res prefix + 3D lift + high-res finish).
Refine Connects to the refine port. Offers three modes: refine (same-resolution refinement), upscale (upscale to target canvas then re-sample according to SIGMAS), and latent_upscale (upscale H3 latent only, no re-sampling).
Report Output Outputs the segment plan and per-segment task summary via the report port.

Model and Configuration Requirements

  • CLIP Loader: The type must be set to minimax (Qwen3-VL).
  • UNET Selection: t2v, i2v, and fl2v tasks use the fl2va UNET. r2v, v2v, and rv2v tasks use the ref2va UNET.
  • Distillation: The model is distilled from FL2VA. Note that r2v, v2v, and rv2v are forced compatibility modes, and caution is advised when using them.
  • ComfyUI Version: Users must upgrade ComfyUI to version 0.30.0 or higher.
  • Source Images: Outputting the original film to source_images fills the independent source_images output without altering the main images output.

🚀 Availability

The complete resource package, including MiniMax H3 model weights and example JSON workflows, is available via Comfyit Stirring Station · Article 506: “MiniMax H3 Models and Workflows.” After downloading, users must merge the models/ directory into ComfyUI/models/. The JSON workflow can be dragged directly into ComfyUI to begin use. The toolbar also supports importing and exporting director packages, which save timeline JSON and reference materials in a zip file.

#MiniMaxH3 #ComfyUI #VideoGeneration #AIVideo #ComfyNodes

Source: AIMixer/ComfyUI_MiniMaxH3_Director

item.title: ComfyUI-Easy-Use Adds Support for Anima and Krea2 Models
item.description:
ComfyUI-Easy-Use Adds Support for Anima and Krea2 Models

ComfyUI-Easy-Use, a custom node integration package for ComfyUI built upon TinyTerraNodes, has added support for Anima and Krea2 diffusion models. The update introduces new nodes and security fixes while enhancing workflow efficiency for various Stable Diffusion model variants.

🧩 How it works

The package integrates and optimizes popular custom nodes to create faster and more convenient workflows, restoring a smooth image production experience similar to traditional Stable Diffusion. Key functional updates include:

  • Anima and Krea2 Support: Enabled via easy diffusionModelLoader and easy XYInputs: DiffusionModel.
  • Loader Requirements: The loader requires an explicit text encoder and VAE selection.
  • Noise Injection: Achieved in latent space using easy latentNoisy or easy preSamplingNoiseIn nodes.
  • Prompt Mode: The loader enables A1111 prompt mode, reproducing images nearly identical to those generated by webui.

⚙️ Key details

Recent additions and fixes to the ComfyUI-Easy-Use package include:

Feature / Update Description
New Nodes Added easy PassOrNone with optional default input and matching types; added easy tableEditor for data editing.
Model Support Supports SD1.x, SD2.x, SDXL, SVD, Zero123, Stable Cascade, Layer Diffuse, InstantID, SD3, Kolors, Flux, Anima, and Krea2.
Security Fixes Fixed style preview path traversal; restricted model downloads to public HTTP(S) addresses; fixed easy saveText to confine outputs to the directory.
Performance Use native VAEDecodeTiled for tiled decode with Qwen Image VAE support.
UI Updates Fixed easy imageChooser inactivity after frontend updates; fixed disabled Alt+1–9 template shortcuts blocking browser shortcuts.

🚀 Availability

Users can install ComfyUI-Easy-Use by cloning the repository into the custom_nodes directory and installing the requirements. For specific integrations like InstantID, the ComfyUI_InstantID package must be present. Layer Diffuse usage may require running pip install -r requirements.txt for dependencies.

#ComfyUI #StableDiffusion #Anima #Krea2 #CustomNodes #AIImageGeneration

item.title: ComfyUI-KJNodes Introduces Enhanced Set/Get Node Functionality
item.description:
ComfyUI-KJNodes Introduces Enhanced Set/Get Node Functionality

🔍 Overview

The ComfyUI-KJNodes project has recently undergone a significant update, introducing enhanced functionalities for Set/Get nodes within the ComfyUI framework. This update focuses on extending support to both legacy and nodes 2.0, alongside promoting cross-subgraph interconnectivity.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Backward Compatibility: The rewrite maintains compatibility with earlier versions, ensuring seamless integration with existing workflows.
  • Subgraph Functionality: Set/Get nodes now operate across parent and child subgraphs, facilitating broader interactions within multi-tiered structures.
  • New Operations:
    • Convert link to Set/Get using a right-click on any link midpoint.
    • Batch convert selected node outputs to Set/Get pairs.
    • The canvas right-click menu supports the conversion of outputs on selected nodes.
  • Key Shortcuts:
    • Ctrl+Shift+S: Add Set nodes.
    • Ctrl+Shift+G: Add Get nodes.
    • Ctrl+Shift+L: Toggle visibility of all connections.
  • Settings Enhancements: New settings for managing link visibility, keyboard shortcuts without conflicting with other actions, and sprite appearance based on connections.
  • Conversion Features: Right-clicking a SetNode adds a corresponding GetNode, and double-clicking a GetNode navigates to its paired SetNode.
  • Type and Color Update: Nodes now reflect type changes when inputs or outputs are disconnected, ensuring consistency in visual feedback.
  • Settings Structure: Settings have been reorganized under KJNodes > Set & Get and KJNodes > General categories for improved navigation.

💡 Why It Matters

This update enhances user interaction and workflow efficiency within the ComfyUI ecosystem. The integration of Set/Get functionalities across subgraphs and the addition of user-friendly features signifies an advancement in customization capabilities, empowering users to build more complex and interconnected AI pipelines.

🚀 Availability

To begin using these features, users should:

  1. Clone the custom_nodes repo to the custom_nodes folder.
  2. Install dependencies using pip install -r requirements.txt.

For portable installs, utilize:

1

custom_setup/ComfyUI_windows_portable-folder/python_embeded/python.exe -m pip install -r ComfyUI/custom_nodes/ComfyUI-KJNodes/requirements.txt

#ComfyUI #AIToolkit #KJNodes #SetGetNodes #Subgraphs #NodeOptimization

item.title: Stability Matrix: Multi-Platform Package Manager and Inference UI for Stable Diffusion
item.description:
Stability Matrix: Multi-Platform Package Manager and Inference UI for Stable Diffusion

Stability Matrix is a multi-platform package manager and inference interface designed for Stable Diffusion. It provides one-click installation and updates for various Stable Diffusion Web UI packages and includes a built-in Inference interface.

🧩 How it Works

  • Package Management: Manages plugins and extensions for supported packages, including Automatic1111, Comfy UI, SD Web UI-UX, and SD.Next.
  • Dependency Handling: Easily installs or updates Python dependencies for each package without requiring global installation of Git or Python.
  • Portability: The application is fully portable; users can move Stability Matrix’s Data Directory to a new drive or computer at any time.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Version Channels: The software is available in Latest Stable, Latest Preview, and Latest Dev versions.
  • Inference Interface: A reimagined interface built into Stability Matrix featuring:
    • Powerful auto-completion and syntax highlighting using a formal language grammar.
    • Workspaces that open in tabs and save/load from .smproj project files.
    • Customizable dockable and float panels.
    • Generated images that contain Inference Project, ComfyUI Nodes, and A1111-compatible data.
  • Documentation: Users can refer to the documentation index for installation, package management, model, and Inference guides. Recommended starting points include generating a first image, importing local models, or managing installed packages.

🚀 Availability

The application supports the following operating systems:

  • Windows 10 and 11
  • Linux (AppImage)
  • Arch Linux (AUR)
  • macOS (Apple Silicon)

Image-to-Video (I2V)

Last Frame Generation

A revolutionary LoRA adapter that transforms AI image generation into cinematic storytelling

Version 2 showcases dramatically improved cinematic flow and visual coherence

next-scene-qwen-image-lora-2509 is a LoRA adapter fine-tuned on Qwen-Image-Edit (build 2509), purpose-built to generate cinematic image sequences with natural visual progression from frame to frame.

This model enables Qwen Image Edit to think like a film director—understanding camera dynamics, visual composition, and narrative continuity to create shots that flow seamlessly into one another.

📦 Version 1 (Legacy)

Model File: next-scene_lora_v1-3000.safetensors ComfyUI Workflow: workflow-comfyui-basic-next-scene.json

V1 Demo Examples:

Version 1 demonstrations showing the foundational cinematic storytelling capabilities

🧠 What This Model Does

This LoRA brings cinematic storytelling continuity into AI image generation workflows.

Each output frame functions as the “Next Scene” in an evolving visual narrative, maintaining compositional coherence while introducing organic transitions such as:

  • Camera movement: Dolly shots, push-ins, pull-backs, and tracking moves
  • Framing evolution: Wide to close-up transitions, angle shifts, reframing
  • Environmental reveals: New characters entering frame, expanded scenery, spatial progression
  • Atmospheric shifts: Lighting changes, weather evolution, time-of-day transitions

Examples of Cinematic Logic:

  • “Next Scene: The camera pulls back from a tight close-up on the airship to a sweeping aerial view, revealing an entire fleet of vessels soaring through a fantasy landscape.”

  • “Next Scene: The camera tracks forward and tilts down, bringing the sun and helicopters closer into frame as a strong lens flare intensifies.”

  • “Next Scene: The camera pans right, removing the dragon and rider from view while revealing more of the floating mountain range in the distance.”

⚙️ Usage Instructions

Basic Setup:

  1. Load Qwen-Image-Edit 2509 as your base model 2. Add a LoRA Loader node and select:
    • V2 (Recommended): next-scene_lora-v2-3000.safetensors
    • V1 (Legacy): next-scene_lora_v1-3000.safetensors 3. Set LoRA strength: 0.7 – 0.8 (recommended)
  2. Structure your prompts with “Next Scene:” prefix for optimal results

Example Prompt: 

1
2

Next Scene: The camera moves slightly forward as sunlight breaks through the clouds, casting a
soft glow around the character's silhouette in the mist. Realistic cinematic style, atmospheric depth.

Pro Tips:

  • Begin prompts with camera direction for stronger continuity
  • Specify lighting and atmospheric changes for mood consistency
  • Chain multiple generations to create sequential storyboards
  • Works particularly well with landscape and establishing shots

🎬 Design Philosophy

Trained on an extensive, curated cinematic dataset (proprietary), this model has learned to think directionally rather than just visually.

It doesn’t simply modify an image—it advances the story, preserving spatial relationships, lighting consistency, and emotional resonance across sequential frames.

Ideal Applications:

  • Storyboard generation for film and animation pre-production
  • Cinematic AI video pipelines requiring frame-to-frame coherence
  • Sequential narrative workflows in ComfyUI and similar tools
  • Concept art evolution showing scene progression
  • Visual storytelling for creative projects and presentations

⚠️ Important Limitations

  • Not optimized for: Static portraits, single-image illustration tasks, or non-sequential edits
  • Best suited for: Multi-frame workflows with narrative progression
  • Design priority: Storytelling flow and continuity over isolated image perfection
  • Recommended use case: Scene-to-scene transitions rather than detailed object manipulation

🧱 Technical Specifications

  • Base Model: Qwen-Image-Edit (build 2509)
  • Architecture: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
  • Training Objective: Scene continuity and cinematic shot coherence
  • Dataset: Large-scale proprietary cinematic imagery
  • Recommended Strength: 0.7–0.8
  • Compatible Platforms: ComfyUI, Automatic1111 (with Qwen support), custom pipelines
